findings.subject: Context spelling does not prove the runtime carrier
findings.disposition: REQUIRED qualification correction; existing FP.CONTEXT owner gate
findings.observation: B4 is correct that nonhook actor/now lower to c.actor/c.now, and team/operation lack named IR arms. Its statement that c.actor/c.now are always bound overstates what the bound c parameter establishes. The actual canonical scenario producer supplies no actor/now/team/operation properties at all.

evidence.fact: Parameter-bound c is described as always-bound c.actor/c.now; nonhook triggers remain E6008.
actor/now become c fields (or hook fields); no team/operation arm.
Example-values fallback becomes a text cell; other unresolved names become IrExpr::Name. Do not generalize free-variable emission to every example cell.
Scope facts are resolver bindings, not producer properties.

HandlerContext/createContext has caller, store, clock, memberships, preferences and optional canonical; canonical has operation:string/operationId:string. It does not supply actor/now/team/operation source-level objects.
Canonical scope carries operation name and admitted operationId, not OperationContext {id,source}.
Actual admitted scenario caller constructs precisely that context and invokes with it.

findings.strongest_countercase: The report may mean only that emitted member expressions have a lexically bound root; another runtime producer might enrich the carrier later. Root already gates all four contextual facts in remaining work. Neither interpretation establishes properties on the inspected serving caller today; this is a qualification correction, not a new carrier architecture choice.
findings.correction: Describe actor/now as emitted member spellings with an unqualified runtime producer; team/operation additionally need verified lowering. Require actor identity/null semantics, fixed admission now, applicable verified team, and readonly operation.id/source to join each owning scope and actual producer before support claims. A canonical operation name or caller/clock property is not equivalent proof.
findings.acceptance: Original required contextual sites compile and execute through the owning admitted carrier; readonly/rejected scope uses and null trusted actor remain qualified; hooks have their separate owner-released bounds. No implementation or option selection performed.

findings.subject: Delivery retry predicate identifies a message token, not the rejected kind
findings.disposition: REQUIRED precise observation and compatibility gate; no demonstrated bypass
findings.observation: The retry tests Error instance, name IncompatibleArtifactError, reason unknown_input_kind and the substring double-quoted delivery anywhere in the message. It does not extract or validate the rejected-kind field. The registry includes the input and operation names in the same message, so a different unknown kind on input named delivery or operation named delivery can satisfy the predicate.

evidence.fact: Message includes("\"delivery\"") is the final predicate.
Error message embeds kind, input name and operation name.
Initial full load and exactly one stripped retry; second failure is not caught by the same retry.

findings.strongest_countercase: A remaining unsupported kind still reaches the same loader on the second pass and should fail; when no delivery descriptors exist the artifact is unchanged. Thus token ambiguity alone does not prove a successful malformed artifact, admission bypass or fallback execution. The bounded retry and propagated second error are real protections.
findings.correction: State exact Error/name/reason/message-token criteria. Keep owner proof that this predicate and the matching descriptor exclusion apply only to the intended compatibility case, rather than claiming semantic delivery-kind provenance from error text.
findings.acceptance: Owner compatibility evidence covers unknown non-delivery kind with delivery-named input/operation, precise retirement with the matching loader, and equally strict transport/admission behavior. Source-only review does not run these witnesses.

findings.subject: Stripped delivery descriptors still need their own integrity proof
findings.disposition: REQUIRED concrete retention/cutover gate; root remaining-work scope supported
findings.observation: stripDeliveryInputs removes every record entry whose nested field.kind equals delivery, with no validation of that removed entry's required/default/tag details. The first registry pass rejects unknown delivery kind before required/default validation and before subsequent duplicate inputs; the retry cannot inspect entries it no longer sees. deliveryFields is retained model schema metadata, a separate contract from removed operation inputs.

evidence.fact: Filter removes nested delivery kind and shallow-copies only touched levels; caller artifact remains unchanged.
Duplicate input is checked in iteration; unknown kind stops before required/default checks for that entry and before later entries.
Loaded descriptors return deliveryFields model map.
New map expectation has three models, each with an empty set; it expressly excludes live observation serving.
Existing shared checker explicitly validates delivery descriptor plus required/default/array/description channels and duplicate input names.
Catalog validates full slice through checkArtifactOperations before excluding delivery from transport framing.

findings.strongest_countercase: There is positive source evidence for the complete preflight owner: interfaces mcp/schemas.ts:722–823 validates delivery descriptors, required/default/array/description channels and duplicates; http/operations.ts:429–446 checks the full slice before excluding delivery. The new HTTP fixture invokes that real derivation (http-operations-route.test.ts:252–268). Full first-pass registry validation retains earlier errors and model schema is not stripped. Therefore the helper does not prove a pipeline validation gap. Retain and qualify this existing single derivation path across actual installed/direct producer joins rather than add a duplicate validator.
findings.correction: Root’s equally-strict integrity/admission gate is supported. Name the existing shared interfaces complete-descriptor validator as the preflight owner and require installed/direct joins to retain it before registry stripping; do not invent duplicate validation. Qualify empty-set deliveryFields assertions as map-shape/whole-model coverage, not positive delivery-tag, association, observation or expiry proof.
findings.acceptance: Actual installed/direct producer evidence retains the existing interfaces complete-descriptor validation before stripping, covering removed delivery tag/required/default/array details and duplicate names; receipt association/current selected leaf and model-tag behavior have separate evidence. The bridge retires when matching loader tolerance is released.

findings.subject: Constructed executable fixtures are not compiler or installed-product evidence
findings.disposition: REQUIRED wording correction; broader no-execution limits confirmed
findings.observation: Replace real emitted labels in the t32b statement with hand-written executable fixture handlers through the canonical seam. They construct create/update/remove and expect history labels create/update/archive; no compiler production occurs in this added test. HTTP source explicitly labels its artifact NOT compiler output, injects the real interfaces dist handlers, and uses MemoryStorage/identity fixtures.

evidence.fact: Fixture string supplies updateRemove handler calling stdlib data plane.
c2Setup writes/loads a constructed module/artifact and fixture storage.
Added invocation expects committed row and create/update/archive history; expectations are not run here.
Header declares hand-written artifact and real handler seam, not compiler output.
OPS_SOURCE/fixture artifact are handwritten; receipt handler records inputs and returns ok.
Real derivation and injected real dist handlers with fixture storage and identity.
Delivery-only input framing records empty inputs, not provider execution or selected receipt association.
HTTP both sealed placement outcomes; MCP malformed tool-level denial, not successful resume proof.
Last conflict/reference case cites earlier pins and directly exercises a positive create only.
Marker and JS string length assertions, not executed export/backend qualification or raw Wasm bytes.
bytes-named module metrics use source string.length, i.e. UTF-16 code units.
Delta only enlarges test timeout from 5s to 30s; no passing result read into this audit.

findings.strongest_countercase: Using real derivation, interfaces dist and canonical invoker makes these meaningful integration expectations rather than mocks of each layer. The fixture directly exercises handler-to-engine execution if run. Root already distinguishes constructed artifacts, installed workerd/D1 and unexecuted expectations; only the compiler-emitted wording and positive-delivery interpretation need narrowing.
findings.correction: Keep source-joined route supersession and substantive fixture scope; call labels expected canonical history labels from constructed handlers. Do not infer compilation, passing results, rich delivery/provider execution, browser draft journey, successful sealed resume or original-app qualification from these bodies.
findings.acceptance: Future owner execution ties compiler-generated original workflows to actual installed producer/assets/auth/state/browser/provider/restart evidence; tests here were read only.
